Measure the space the job needs

By v/hNovember 16, 2026Document

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

A small device can still take over a countertop.

Imagine a compact utility with a lid that opens backwards. It fits on a shallow shelf when closed, but using it means pulling it forward and moving whatever is beside it.

An early size check should include the space needed to load it, reach the controls, remove the result and route the cable. Any required ventilation clearance belongs in that measurement too.

A proposed prototype check would use ordinary locations with their other objects left in place. Record what the person has to move, whether they can complete the job comfortably, and what space remains usable afterwards. Repeat with the tool or routine the person uses today.

For v/h, adding a local model, sensors and cooling must earn the room they occupy. The better result should still be available where the owner actually needs it.

Our first utility is in development. The devices described and drawn are illustrative, and the document describes proposed checks.
